name: jig_trust_pilot2
about: Pilot 2 (14 Nov 2026), locked once before any build and not changed after. How far can a Jig way of building software be trusted, and which parts of the script earn their place? Four founders = spec format (prose, facts) x builder (opus = Claude Opus through Claude Code, luna = GPT-6 Luna through Codex); Claude Opus always writes the spec and does the verifying. OPUS_PROSE is the control: the game factory as it works today. Compare: 6 harder briefs written for pilot 2 (poker hands, reversi, checkers, Go capture rules, cribbage counting, chess move legality), because in pilot 1 (a dry run) every founder passed every check of the easier briefs. Take apart: the script itself on the same 6 briefs; parts = spec format and three steps as switches (the test step, the verify step, the fix rounds), each alternative the step switched off; all 16 combinations. Build out: one round in which the designer (Claude Opus, no tools, firewalled brief) writes 2 versions each of two text parts (an extra rule for the spec writer, extra notes for the builder), screened on 3 fresh briefs and confirmed on 3 more. Sealed: the 6 sealed briefs written before pilot 1 and never opened. Every brief has 6 hidden acceptance checks, frozen (jig_trust/frozen.py) and proven on a reference implementation (check_references.py). Score: 1 per hidden check passed; the 6 checks of a brief form a cluster. Too small to be a result: a pilot of the bridge, with a first trust score.
